html:
The massacre of Salsipuedes was an attack on the Charrúa people by the army of Uruguay on 11 April 1831, at Salsipuedes creek. It destroyed the last free Charrúa communities.

The Charrúa had lived as hunters on the grasslands for centuries and fought for Artigas. The new government of President Fructuoso Rivera, wanting the land for ranches, lured them to a meeting with promises of friendship, then attacked. Dozens were killed and hundreds of women and children were taken and given as servants in Montevideo.

In 1833 four survivors were shipped to Paris and shown to the public; all died there. For a long time Uruguay described itself as a country without Indigenous people. In recent decades descendants have asked for recognition, and the remains of the chief Vaimaca Perú were brought home from France in 2002.
